name: Massachusetts
nameStory: From the Massachusett people, meaning roughly 'at the great hill' - the Blue Hills just south of Boston. The longest, most misspelled state name in America is really just directions to a hill you can still go climb.
capitalStory: Boston was built on a cramped, hilly peninsula, so colonists did something drastic: they shoveled the hills into the harbor to manufacture more land. Much of downtown Boston, including Back Bay, is ground that did not exist in 1700.

majorFeatures.name: Cape Cod
majorFeatures.note: A pile of sand and gravel dumped by a glacier

majorFeatures.name: Connecticut River
majorFeatures.note: Splits the state's fertile middle valley

funFacts: America's first public school (Boston Latin, 1635) and first college (Harvard, 1636) are both here, founded within a year of each other.
Boston opened the first subway in the United States in 1897.
Cape Cod is a glacial moraine - it only exists because an ice sheet stopped there and dropped its load of rubble.
Basketball and volleyball were both invented in Massachusetts, in Springfield and Holyoke.
whyItMatters: The Boston Massacre, the Tea Party, and the first shots at Lexington and Concord all happened within a few dozen miles of each other. The American Revolution began as a local Massachusetts quarrel that spread.
